title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Laboratory Knowledge & Skills - Biotechnology - Equipment calibration & validation
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: To strictly adhere to Good Laboratory Practices (GLP), a technician must validate the volumetric accuracy of a P1000 micropipette prior to an audited biomanufacturing run. They set the dial to $1000 \ \mu\text{L}$ and dispense high-purity deionized water onto an analytical balance at standard room temperature ($22^\circ\text{C}$). According to gravimetric calibration principles, what specific mass should the analytical balance display if the pipette is perfectly calibrated?
questions.explain:
**Gravimetric calibration** relies on the known physical density of water. 

At standard room temperature, the density of pure liquid water is extremely close to $1.0 \text{ g/mL}$. Because $1000 \ \mu\text{L}$ is exactly equal to $1.0 \text{ mL}$, pipetting this volume of water onto an analytical balance should yield a mass of precisely **$1.000 \text{ g}$**. If the balance consistently reads significantly higher or lower (e.g., $0.950 \text{ g}$), the pipette is out of calibration.

questions.q: Before preparing chemical buffers, a technician must perform a routine multi-point calibration on a laboratory pH meter using traceable standard solutions. What is the fundamental scientific purpose of utilizing a **three-point calibration** ($pH\ 4.0, 7.0, \text{ and } 10.0$) rather than simply calibrating the meter exclusively with neutral deionized water ($pH\ 7.0$)?
options: To permanently alter the internal electrical resistance of the glass electrode to match room temperature.
To physically sterilize the sensitive glass bulb from acidophilic and alkaliphilic bacteria.
To establish a linear slope across a wide pH range, ensuring the meter can accurately calculate measurements in both acidic and basic unknown samples.
To saturate the internal silver chloride reference solution so the electrode does not dry out during the week.
questions.explain:
A pH meter measures the tiny voltage difference created by hydrogen ions and calculates the pH based on a mathematical formula (the Nernst equation). 

By testing three known points ($4.0$, $7.0$, $10.0$), the meter's internal software can calculate a precise **linear slope (calibration curve)**. If calibrated *only* at $pH\ 7.0$ (a single-point calibration), the meter has no reference line and cannot accurately determine if an unknown sample is highly acidic or highly basic. It only knows what neutral is.

questions.q: A standard autoclave uses pressurized steam ($121^\circ\text{C}$ at $15 \text{ psi}$) to achieve absolute sterilization of media and equipment. To routinely validate that the autoclave is functioning correctly and actually achieving lethal sterilizing conditions, which specific Quality Control (QC) indicator must the laboratory deploy?
options: Striped autoclave indicator tape affixed to the outside of every flask
Biological indicator vials containing *Geobacillus stearothermophilus* endospores
A digital countdown timer verified by a secondary atomic clock
A visual inspection of the agar for boiling bubbles immediately upon removal
questions.explain:
To truly validate sterilization, the laboratory must prove lethality, not just heat exposure. 

Autoclave tape (Option 'a') is a *chemical* indicator; its stripes turn black when exposed to high heat, but this happens almost instantly and does not prove the heat lasted long enough to kill microbes. **Biological indicators (BIs)** containing the highly heat-resistant endospores of *Geobacillus stearothermophilus* are placed in the load. If these extremely tough spores are killed, it proves the autoclave successfully achieved true sterilization parameters.
